content: Straight, Incorporated was a nationally recognized non-profit organization that operated as a drug rehabilitation program. Over its 15 years of operation, it became the subject of numerous reports detailing allegations of abuse inflicted on adolescents and their families. Despite these allegations, which included testimonies from individuals who had escaped the program and ongoing lawsuits, Straight, Inc. received significant praise within Republican political circles during its existence. The organization was founded on April 22, 1976, by Mel Sembler, and its treatment program officially began on September 1, 1976. The program employed a controversial therapeutic approach known as tough love, which has been compared to methods of brainwashing. This approach, along with the numerous allegations of abuse and legal actions, ultimately led to the closure of Straight, Inc. in July 1993. In the years following the program's dissolution, many former patients have come together to form survivor groups. These groups consist of small gatherings of individuals who seek to process and understand the trauma they endured during their time in the program. They also provide mutual support to one another as they attempt to come to terms with the reality of their experiences.
